summary: Nicolae Ceaușescu, communist dictator of Romania from 1965 to 1989, won Western favour while building a vast surveillance state and palace, banning abortion and starving the population, until he and his wife Elena were executed in 1989.

evidence.note: birth in January 1918 in a poor village; long Romanian history preamble ends here
teenage arrests for street fights at strikes and petitions for rail workers
Gheorghiu-Dej dies in March 1965 and Ceausescu takes the party leadership
1968 balcony speech condemning the Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia; ties with Nixon
1971 tour of China and North Korea inspires the personality cult and industrial push
regime sells exit visas for Romanian Jews on a sliding price scale
Securitate phone tapping and informant network expand; assassinations abroad
preventable deaths and neglect of children in state homes for disabled children
untested blood transfusions spread HIV among orphans, most of them Roma
summary trial and execution of the couple on Christmas Day 1989

notes: Part 1 spends about 40 minutes on Romanian background (Dacia, Vlad the Impaler, 1907 peasant revolt, WWI, Iron Guard); treated as scene-setting, so covered_span follows the lifetime rule. Elena is secondary since the title centres Nicolae, though she gets long segments. Her birth year (1916) is from general knowledge. Post-1989 orphan aftermath is a short coda. No theme for trophy hunting or reproductive policy.
